Abstract
A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization (LC-APCI-MS). This study employs high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to a quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer (HPLC-QTOF MS) to analyze the secondary metabolites produced by *C. nivalis*. Specifically, this approach focuses on the detection and characterization of astaxanthin diglucoside diesters, which have not been previously identified in this algal species. The use of atmospheric pressure chemical ionization (APCI) enables the generation of molecular ions through proton transfer, facilitating the accurate determination of molecular weights and fragmentation patterns that distinguish between isomeric compounds. The results provide novel insights into the biosynthetic pathways and potential ecological roles of these unique metabolites in polar environments.

raw_response.text: Skin biopsy homogenates obtained from three cases of lepromatous leprosy with no prior history of antileprosy treatment were tested in the mouse footpad for the sensitivity of Mycobacterium leprae to multiple drugs. This study aimed to investigate the primary drug resistance patterns of M. leprae in untreated lepromatous leprosy patients, as well as to assess the susceptibility profiles when individual drugs were tested in combination. The results revealed a spectrum of resistance to first-line drugs ( rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone), indicating the presence of primary resistance. Furthermore, synergistic and antagonistic effects were observed among different combinations of these drugs, highlighting the complexity of therapeutic strategies against M. leprae. These findings underscore the importance of early and accurate drug sensitivity testing to guide effective treatment protocols for leprosy. The mouse footpad model served as an efficient in vivo assay system, providing insights into the pathogenesis and drug resistance mechanisms of leprosy at its primary site of infection.

raw_response.text: As a member of the testis-specific serine/threonine protein kinase (TSSK) family, Tssk4 is exclusively expressed in the testis and plays an essential role in male fertility. We previously reported that Tssk4 is involved in spermatogenesis through the regulation of sperm tail development, but the specific mechanisms underlying its function remain largely unknown. In this study, we focused on elucidating the molecular mechanism by which Tssk4 modulates male fertility. We found that Tssk4 directly phosphorylates Odf2 (Outer Dense Fiber Protein 2) at Ser-76. Our results demonstrate that this phosphorylation event significantly enhances the interaction between Odf2 and its binding partner, the dynein intermediate chain (Dyic). The enhanced interaction subsequently leads to the proper localization and organization of outer dense fibers, which are crucial for the assembly and motility of the sperm flagellum. Moreover, we observed that Tssk4-deficient mice exhibit impaired sperm motility, further supporting the importance of Odf2 phosphorylation by Tssk4 in male fertility.

raw_response.text: A simple shock event approach inspired by the Allende meteorite to produce sophisticated carbon nanomaterials is reported. It is demonstrated that unique carbon nanostructures, including carbon nanotubes, carbon onions, and new carbon nanorings are synthesized through this method. The synthesis process mimics the high-pressure and high-temperature conditions encountered during cosmic collisions, effectively leveraging the mechanical and thermal characteristics of shock waves generated in such events. This novel technique not only simplifies the production of various carbon nanomaterials but also provides insights into the natural formation of similar structures observed in extraterrestrial materials. The results suggest promising applications in advanced material science, energy storage, catalysis, and nanotechnology.

raw_response.text: The case of a young female patient with acute symmetrical ascending polyneuropathy as a manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is reported. There was involvement of several cranial nerves, including the facial, glossopharyngeal, vagus, and accessory nerves, indicating a multifocal neuropathic process. The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed elevated protein levels (102 mg/dL; normal range 15-45 mg/dL) with a mild pleocytosis (10 cells/µL; normal range <10 cells/µL). Anti-GQ1b antibodies were negative, ruling out Guillain-Barré syndrome of the Miller Fisher variant. The patient also presented with malar rash, oral ulcers, and photosensitivity, consistent with an SLE diagnosis. Comprehensive immunosuppressive therapy with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and corticosteroids led to partial recovery of neurologic function within 6 weeks, though residual weakness persisted.

raw_response.text: This paper presents experimental dependences of the width of the reaction zone and detonation critical diameter on the initial density with a variation in the density of an emulsion high explosive from 0.5 to 1.33 g/cm³. Glass tubes were used as experimental containers to study the propagation characteristics of the detonation wave. The experiments involved preparing emulsion explosives at different densities through varying the concentration of the oil phase and aqueous phase while maintaining consistent chemical composition. High-speed camera techniques were employed to record the propagation of the detonation wave and analyze the width of the reaction zone. Additionally, impulse gauges were utilized to measure the pressure wavefront velocity and further confirm the critical diameter conditions for detonation initiation. The results demonstrate that there is a significant linear relationship between the initial density and the width of the reaction zone, with the detonation critical diameter also varying inversely with density.

raw_response.text: In this article, we develop a model of the interactions between the revenue management (RM) practices of competing airlines. The theoretical model is supported by simulation results from Passenger Origin and Destination Simulator (PODS), highlighting the critical role of passenger spill between airlines on optimal RM seat allocations in competitive markets. Our analysis reveals that the interplay of demand forecasting, overbooking strategies, and competitive pricing dynamics significantly affects revenue outcomes for airlines. We introduce a novel framework that incorporates passenger cross-elasticity and dynamic pricing adjustments, demonstrating how these factors influence seat allocation decisions and overall market performance. The simulation results provide empirical evidence that strategic considerations of competitive interactions can lead to more sophisticated and nuanced RM policies, ultimately impacting profitability and customer satisfaction.

raw_response.text: We investigated how people use base rates and sample size information when integrating data from multiple sources to make overall probability judgments. Participants considered two samples from an animal population in order to estimate the probability of that animal being aggressive. Participants' judgments were influenced by subpopulation base rates and sample sizes, but the extent to which each factor influenced judgments varied depending on the representativeness of the samples. Our results demonstrate that when samples are highly representative of the population, participants rely more heavily on base rates, whereas with less representative samples, judgments become more sensitive to sample sizes.

raw_response.text: Abstract The photon decay of the relativistic Coulomb excitation of the double Giant Dipole Resonance (GDR) in the target has been observed in a 1 A GeV 209Bi beam incident on a 208Pb target. The photon spectrometer recorded the energy and angular distribution of the emitted photons, providing insights into the collective properties of the excited nuclear system. By analyzing these data, we have investigated the structure and dynamics of the 2-phonon GDR in 208Pb. Our findings reveal the role of two-phonon configurations in the excitation spectrum and offer new information on the coupling strength between the phonon modes and the collective oscillations of the nuclear matter.
